Package index

Ask a question

Start here. One call reads a document and answers a question, and the answer says what it rests on and whether anything went wrong. See vignette("harnessr").

answer_document()
Answer a question about a document
gr_answer
The result of one reading run
is_not_found()
Did the model report that the document does not contain the answer?
gr_example()
Path to the bundled example document
gr_recipes()
Ready-made recipes
gr_recipe()
Bind an ingestion, segmentation and reading configuration together
gr_compare()
Run several recipes over one document and compare them

Connect to a model

Clients for OpenAI-compatible endpoints, any provider ellmer supports, any function you write, and an offline stand-in for practice and tests. See vignette("harnessr") and the README.

gr_client()
Construct a model client
gr_api_key()
Resolve the API key
gr_ellmer_client()
Read documents through an ellmer chat
gr_backend_client()
Use any function as the model transport
gr_mock_client()
A deterministic offline client for tests, demos and dry runs
gr_call()
Call a model
gr_result
The result of one model call
gr_models()
List every known model
gr_model_info()
Look up a model's capabilities
gr_model_limits()
Context and output limits for a model
gr_register_model()
Register a model (or override a built-in entry)

Get text out of files

Extraction, cleaning and a survey of a folder before anything is spent. See vignette("ingest").

gr_ingest()
Ingest a document into cleaned, provenance-bearing text blocks
gr_ingest_spec()
Describe an ingestion configuration
gr_document
An ingested document
gr_extractors()
List registered extractors
gr_cleaners()
List registered cleaners
gr_clean()
Run the cleaning pipeline over a character vector
gr_inventory()
What is in a folder, before you read any of it

Cut documents into chunks

The segmenters, their settings, and the free statistics for comparing chunkings. See vignette("segment").

gr_segment()
Segment a document into chunks
gr_segment_spec()
Describe a segmentation configuration
gr_segmenters()
List registered segmentation strategies
gr_chunks
A set of document chunks
gr_chunk_stats()
Summary statistics for a chunk set

Read the chunks

The reading strategies, the settings that choose and place chunks, and the check on quoted evidence. See vignette("readers").

gr_read()
Read chunks and answer a question
gr_read_spec()
Describe a reading configuration
gr_readers()
List registered reading strategies
gr_reader_signature()
The traversal signature of a reader
gr_embed()
Embed texts
gr_embedders()
List registered embedding backends
gr_verify_evidence()
Check that quoted evidence really is in the document

Many documents and literature reviews

One question over many documents, and a review from a search export to screened studies, an extraction table, a written review and an audit report, with the screening measured against a hand-screened sample. See vignette("review").

gr_read_many()
Ask one question of many documents
gr_protocol()
Write down what a review is looking for
gr_protocols()
Protocols that ship with the package, and any you have registered
gr_protocol_save() gr_protocol_read()
Save a protocol to a file, and read one back
gr_register_protocol()
Register a protocol
gr_search()
Record how the search was run
gr_records()
Read a search export, and say what the search found
gr_screen()
Decide which documents a review should read
gr_reference()
Draw a sample to screen by hand
gr_reference_consensus()
Form one decision per document from several reviewers
gr_calibrate()
Measure the screener against a hand-screened sample
gr_screen_sample_size()
How many records to judge by hand to show a recall target
gr_resolve()
Record a person's decision on screened records
`[`(<gr_reference_frame>)
Subsetting a reference frame gives a plain data frame.
gr_fields()
Build an extraction schema
gr_field()
Describe one field of an extraction schema
gr_extract()
Extract a typed schema from many documents
gr_extract_agreement()
Agreement between two extraction tables, field by field
gr_claims()
The claims a table of studies supports
gr_outline()
Derive a review's sections from its claims
gr_outline_pick()
Choose one of the outlines gr_outline() compared
gr_gaps()
What a body of work does not cover
gr_synthesise()
Write a review from an extraction table
gr_flow()
Count what happened to every document
gr_audit_report()
Write the run out as an auditable report

Cost, limits and tracing

Settings and spending limits, token counts and cost estimates, and the trace every run records. See vignette("runs").

gr_options()
Get or set package options
hr_governor()
Limits on what a run may send
gr_estimate_cost()
Estimate the USD cost of a set of calls
gr_count_tokens()
Count tokens in text
gr_tokenizer()
The active tokenizer
gr_set_tokenizer()
Register or inspect the active tokenizer
gr_truncate_tokens()
Truncate text to at most n tokens
gr_budget()
Compute a usable input-token budget for one model call
gr_trace() as.data.frame(<gr_trace>)
Create a run trace
gr_trace_summary()
Summarise a trace
gr_trace_cost()
What a run actually cost
gr_trace_save()
Save a trace to a file
as_json()
Serialise an object to JSON

Caching and replaying runs

Paying for a request once, and replaying a recorded run without a model. See vignette("runs").

gr_cache()
A response cache
gr_cache_client()
Attach a cache to a client
gr_cache_stats()
Cache statistics
gr_cache_clear()
Delete every entry in a cache
gr_flush_caches()
Clear the session's document and embedding caches
gr_replay_client()
A client that answers from a recorded run

Statistics

Intervals for proportions, agreement between raters and coders, design-weighted and prediction-powered estimates, and the test of whether a model’s labels can stand in for people’s. See vignette("evaluate").

hr_prop_ci()
Confidence intervals for binomial proportions
hr_agreement()
Agreement between raters, with every measure that should go with it
hr_ht_estimate()
Design-weighted estimates from a probability sample
hr_ppi()
Prediction-powered inference for a mean
hr_alt_test()
The alternative annotator test

Benchmarks

Compare configurations on a labelled reference: arms, the reference and its splits, scorers, and repeated runs held to one spending limit. See vignette("evaluate").

hr_benchmark() print(<hr_bench>)
Run arms against a reference
hr_report() print(<hr_bench_report>) as_json(<hr_bench_report>)
Report a benchmark with intervals
hr_mdd() hr_n_needed() print(<hr_mdd>) print(<hr_n_needed>)
The minimum detectable difference of a paired, clustered design
hr_contrast() hr_register_contrasts() print(<hr_contrast>) print(<hr_contrast_registration>)
Non-inferiority contrasts, registered before scoring
hr_drift_check() print(<hr_drift_check>)
Check an arm for drift against a frozen benchmark
hr_arm()
A configuration to compare in a benchmark
hr_reference() hr_reference_add()
A reference set to score arms against
hr_scorer() hr_scorer_exact()
A rule for scoring an arm's output
gr_arm() gr_arms()
A reading recipe as an arm of a benchmark
gr_qa_reference()
A reference of questions about documents
gr_scorer_answer()
Score a reading recipe's answer against acceptable answers

Baselines

Comparisons that use no model: tf-idf features, a cross-fitted classifier, a simulated active-learning ranker for screening, and the stopping test for prioritised screening. See vignette("evaluate"), and vignette("review") for the stopping test.

hr_tfidf()
Tf-idf features from texts
hr_baseline_classifier() print(<hr_baseline_classifier>)
Cross-fitted text classifier baseline
hr_baseline_ranker() print(<hr_baseline_ranker>)
Active-learning screening baseline
gr_stop_test() print(<gr_stop_test>)
Hypergeometric stopping test for prioritised screening

Judges

A model that chooses between candidates or grades one against a reference, asked in both orders, validated against blind human labels before it scores, with its accuracy corrected by those labels. See vignette("evaluate").

hr_judge() print(<hr_judgement>)
Judge candidates with a model, in more than one order
hr_judge_config() print(<hr_judge_config>)
A judge configuration
hr_judge_validate() hr_judge_valid() print(<hr_judge_validation>)
Validate a judge against blind human labels
hr_scorer_judge()
Score benchmark runs with a validated judge
hr_judge_ppi()
Judge-scored accuracy corrected with human labels

Signals and calibration

Values the package records about its own work, the calibration records that measure how well they predict being right, and the thresholds and policy that decide whether a signal may gate an action. Nothing gates by default. See vignette("evaluate").

hr_signal() hr_signals()
Record a self-signal
hr_calibrate_signal()
Calibrate a self-signal against graded items
hr_calibration_valid()
Is a calibration record valid for a run?
hr_gate_threshold()
Choose a gate threshold by Learn-then-Test
hr_signal_policy() hr_apply_signal()
What a signal may do, and what happens when it may not

Reference sets and splits

Splitting reference items into tuning, calibration and test sets by document, and the sheets people fill in to label them. See vignette("evaluate").

hr_assign_splits()
Assign reference items to splits by cluster
gr_label_sheet()
Write a sheet for people to label
gr_read_labels()
Read a filled label sheet

Extending harnessr

Every axis is a registry, and an addition is used exactly like a built-in. See vignette("extending").

gr_register_extractor()
Register a document extractor
gr_register_cleaner()
Register a cleaning step
gr_register_segmenter()
Register a segmentation strategy
gr_register_reader()
Register a reading strategy
gr_register_embedder()
Register an embedding backend
new_chunks()
Build a gr_chunks, the object every segmenter must return
new_answer()
Build a gr_answer, the object every reader must return
hr_cost()
What one run of a module can cost
hr_schema()
Collect parameters into a schema
hr_param()
Declare one parameter of a module or spec
hr_validate()
Validate and resolve settings against a schema
hr_check_module()
Check a module against a set of rules
gr_check_reader()
Check a reader against the reader contract
gr_check_segmenter()
Check a segmenter against the segmenter contract

Superseded

The entry points of the first version, and the old name of gr_example(). They still work and warn once; new code should use answer_document(), gr_ingest(), gr_segment() and gr_example(). The README’s “Migrating from v1” section maps each one.

answer_question()
Deprecated: answer a question using v1 mode names
parse_text()
Deprecated: parse a document into text chunks
gpt_read_chunked()
Deprecated: chunk-by-chunk reading
gpt_read_hierarchical()
Deprecated: hierarchical reading
gpt_read_multipass()
Deprecated: multi-pass reading
gpt_read_retrieval()
Deprecated: evidence-extraction reading
readgpt_example()
Deprecated: path to the bundled example document
